$about: The Labs page (examples/labs.html, my-3d2dge.vercel.app/labs) is built from this list by tools/build.mjs, in the list's order. check (To check) holds what only the owner can judge (feel, sound, a real phone): each entry says what to do (what) and what to look for (look), its title opening the place (at: what to add to the address); it goes once checked. Each section has a title (short: a shorter name for the bar at the top, if it needs one), a line saying what it holds (about) and its entries; line: true numbers them, one line in the order it was made, each with made (when it was made). Each entry is one page: page is an examples/ page name (examples/<page>.html, served at /<page>) or a dist/ path; its title opens the page, and links are other places to start, [label, what to add to the address] (or another dist/ path). line, kits and keep (Tools) are kept. temporary holds the prototypes (DOCTRINE.md) in the order they were made, one-off comparisons and experiments, each with the date it was added and the question it answers; next: the page it led to, and deviates: one line for each way it departs from the doctrine, if any. When the question is settled, delete the page and its entry, or graduate it to another section (it is then held to the engine tier). A change to a prototype alone needs no version bump. tools/labs-test.mjs opens every link.

sections.title: To check
sections.about: What only a person can judge: how it feels in the hands, how it sounds, how it plays on a real phone. Each card says what to do and what to look for, and its button opens the place. Tell Claude what you find (a line is enough); a card goes once it is checked.

entries.title: Roguelike on your phone
entries.what: Open it on your phone and play a floor or two: tap a cell to walk there, hold the stick to step, WAIT, POTION and SCROLL at the side. Added with v0.63.0 (Milestone 2).
entries.look: Does a tap walk where you meant? Are the buttons in reach of a thumb? Can you read the crypt in the dark (the torchlight, the fog over what you saw before)? Does a run feel fair: bats twice your speed, slimes half?

entries.title: Puzzle: how the blocks handle
entries.what: Play BLOCKS for a few minutes with the keys (arrows, Space drop, C hold), then on your phone (drag, tap, flick down, flick up); then a round of PAIRS. Added with v0.63.0 (Milestone 2).
entries.look: Does it handle like a modern Tetris: the auto-shift when you hold a side, the turn by a wall (kicks), time to slide a piece once it lands? On the phone, does a flick drop or hold every time, and never by mistake? In PAIRS, does a chain feel worth it?

entries.title: Arcade: do the three classics feel right?
entries.what: Play each cabinet for a few minutes, on the keys or a pad (arrows, Space fires; in ROCKS up thrusts, X warps), then once on your phone. Press C (a pad's Y) in a game to switch to the classic look and back. Lose all your lives once to see the continue, the letter wheel and the table; leave the cabinet alone for 20 seconds to see the demo. Added with v0.64.0 (Milestone 3).
entries.look: MAZE: does a turn pressed early happen at the next corner, and do the four wisps feel different (one chases, one cuts you off, one flanks, one is shy)? FORMATION: do the dives look like Galaga's swoops, and is it fair? ROCKS: do thrust and drift feel weighty, and do the glowing lines read well? Is the remaster or the classic look better, and are the cabinet's sides too busy?

entries.title: Shooter: the horizontal stage
entries.what: Play stage 2 to its end: pick up the red capsules and press X (or POWER on a phone) to take the lit power on the bar at the bottom; get a couple of OPTIONs and watch them trail you; beat the cruiser and the core behind its walls. Then play the vertical stage from the start to see it lead into stage 2. Added with v0.64.0 (Milestone 3).
entries.look: Does it feel like Gradius: the power bar's choices, the options following your path, the rock you must not touch? Is it too hard or too easy (the core, the cavern's guns)? Is the cavern readable on your phone, with the bar above the touch area?

entries.title: Brawler with a friend
entries.what: Start the fight, then a friend presses 2 to drop in on the keyboard's right half (arrows move, . punches, / kicks, , sweeps, L jumps); you move to the left half (WASD, F punch, G kick, H sweep, R jump). Or plug in a gamepad and press its Start to drop in on it. Play the first two waves together, and press Backspace (player 2's pause) once. Added with v0.65.0 (Milestone 4).
entries.look: Is sharing the keyboard comfortable, or do your hands collide? Does the camera keep both of you in view without jumping? Can you tell your hero from your friend's (Max in white and red, Jack in blue) in a crowd? Does the round card show each player's keys, and does the pause say P2 PAUSED?

entries.title: Puzzle versus
entries.what: With a friend: press 2 so the friend joins (or Start on a gamepad), then pick VERSUS (W and S move the cursor, F picks). Player 1 plays on WASD with F to turn, H to drop and R to hold; player 2 on the arrows with . to turn, , to drop and L to hold. Clear two rows or more at once to send rows to the other field. Added with v0.65.0 (Milestone 4).
entries.look: Do the rows you send feel like an attack (the red bar beside the other field, then grey rows rising at its next piece)? Is it clear who won? Are the two fields big enough on a laptop screen?

entries.title: Fighting: does it feel like Street Fighter?
entries.what: In training (the button opens it), pick RYO and try his specials on the dummy: down, down-forward, forward and a punch (U) for a fireball; forward, down, down-forward and HP (I) for the uppercut; down, down-back, back and HK (K) for the spinning kick. Tab changes the dummy (stand, crouch, jump, guard). Then play ARCADE through its three fights, and VERSUS with a friend or a pad. Added with v0.66.0 (Milestone 4).
entries.look: Do the motions come out when you mean them, and never when you don't? Does a hit feel solid (the stop, the spark, the crowd) and a block feel safe? Are the three fighters different enough (RYO balanced, GORM slow and strong, VEX quick)? Is the CPU fair at each stage? On your phone, do the stick and the four buttons work, quarter circles included?

entries.title: Metroidvania: does it feel like Super Metroid?
entries.what: Play from the landing site (the button opens it): right through the caverns (crouch with down to crawl under the rock), down the flooded shaft into the shrine for the SPRING BOOTS, back up the vine to the save room, through the green hatch and up the tower to the beetle; its dash opens the blue hatch to the laboratory, the lift and the reactor's boss. Arrows move and aim, Space jumps (twice, with the boots), X fires (hold it to charge), E lashes, Shift dashes, Q held stands still to aim, Tab shows the map. The other buttons go straight to the two boss fights (with the abilities given) and to the map. Added with v0.67.0 (Milestone 5).
entries.look: Do the moves feel right: the jump's height, the ledge you catch, crawling, swimming, the vine, the monkey bars, the walls you cling to? Does aiming eight ways and the charged shot feel like Metroid? Does a room's door slide you into the next cleanly, and does the map fill in as you go? Are the bosses fair (the beetle jumped as it charges, then shot from behind; the eye shot while it is open)? Does a save bring you back where you saved? On your phone: the stick (it aims too), JUMP, FIRE (it lashes beside a foe) and MAP.

entries.title: Kart: does it feel like Super Mario Kart?
entries.what: Race three laps against five (the button starts it): up or Z is the gas, down or X brakes, left and right steer; tap Space as you turn into a bend and hold it to drift (sparks blue, then orange: let go for a boost); drive through a ? box for an item and fire it with E (a boost, a shell that flies ahead, a peel dropped behind). Then VS with a friend: press 2 (or Start on a pad), and the screen splits. Added with v0.69.0 (Milestone 6).
entries.look: Does the Mode 7 track feel right: the floor turning under you, the sky turning with it, the karts and trees growing as you near them? Does the kart grip in a bend, slide in a drift, and does the drift boost feel earned? Do the other drivers race you (braking for bends, passing, spinning out on a shell) without getting stuck? Is the race close? On your phone: it drives itself forward; the stick steers; DRIFT and ITEM.

entries.title: Road: does it feel like OutRun?
entries.what: Pick a song on the radio (left and right, then Enter), then drive to the goal before the clock runs out (the button opens the radio): up or Z is the gas, down or X brakes, Space changes gear (LOW pulls away hard, HIGH runs to 290), left and right steer. Each CHECKPOINT arch gives time back. The beach, the hills, a tunnel through the cliffs, the desert at dusk, the city at night. Added with v0.69.0 (Milestone 6).
entries.look: Does the road feel fast and smooth: the curves throwing you outward, the hills hiding what is past them, the tunnel? Do you have to slow (or drop to low gear) for the hardest bends? Are the palms, rocks and signs fair to dodge, and the traffic? Is the clock tight but fair? On your phone: it drives itself forward; the stick steers; BRAKE and GEAR.

entries.title: RPG: does it feel like Dragon Quest and Final Fantasy?
entries.what: Start a New game and play the journey: talk to the people of Brightwater (Enter or Z talks and reads on, L or E opens the MENU), take the elder's quest, shop, try Equip in the MENU, open the chest, save at the crystal. Leave by the south gate and walk the road north across the island: fights come at random (in a fight, L turns on AUTO). Train a little, enter the cave in the peaks, find its crystal, and face the Dread Knight. Then pick Continue or Load on the title. Added with v0.71.0 (Milestone 7).
entries.look: Does the town feel alive: the elder's '!', the child's song, the guard stepping aside, the markup in the lines (color, pauses, a shaking voice)? Is the walking pleasant, and are encounters too often or too rare? Does a level-up feel earned, and is the knight a fair fight at level 2 or 3? Do the menus read well (Items, Equip with its + and -, Status, Quests, the save slots)? On your phone: the stick walks, TALK and MENU, taps in every window.

entries.title: TACTICS: does it feel like Final Fantasy Tactics and Fire Emblem?
entries.what: Watch the scene at the fort (Enter reads on, X skips), pick how the turns run (by speed, or by phases), and take Thornwatch. On a turn: MOVE (a blue cell), ATTACK or the skill (a red cell; gold shows what it hits), then WAIT and face a way; X undoes a move before you act. Q and E turn the view, the wheel zooms; the mouse moves the cursor. Strike from behind and from above; keep out of the river; mind the archer on the wall and the mage's fire. Added with v0.72.0 (Milestone 8).
entries.look: Can you always tell which cell the cursor is on, even on the walls and the tower, and after turning the view? Do the ranges read at a glance, and do the blows from behind and from above feel worth the trouble? Is the Legion's AI a fair fight (does it gang up, heal, flank, hold the high ground)? Is a battle too long or too short? On your phone: a tap selects, a tap moves, a tap strikes; a drag pans; TURN; are the rows easy to hit?

entries.title: RTS: does it feel like Warcraft II and StarCraft?
entries.what: Build up the Vale and burn the Ash Clan's camp across the river. Your workers mine on their own; click the hall (or H) and train more (Z). Click a worker, then BARRACKS (Z) and a place for it; later a STABLE. Train footmen, archers and knights; drag a box round them (or R for the whole army), right click to send them, F then a click to fight their way there. The clan's first wave comes at about four minutes. The minimap (bottom right) moves the camera; arrows, WASD and the screen's edge pan it; the wheel zooms. Added with v0.74.0 (Milestone 9).
entries.look: Does selecting and ordering feel right (a click, a box, Shift, a double click for every one of a kind, Ctrl and a digit for a group)? Do armies move as a body and find their way round the woods and over the fords, without piling up? Is the gold coming in too fast or too slow, and is the clan's first wave a fair test? Can you read a battle (who is hurt, who is yours)? On your phone: a tap selects or orders, a drag pans, a long press and a drag draws a box, two fingers zoom; HALL, ARMY and IDLE; BUILD then a tap and PLACE.

entries.title: SIM: does it feel like Theme Park and RollerCoaster Tycoon?
entries.what: Grow Sunny Bay Park from its carousel and burger stand. PATH (Q) then click a tile or drag a line; build the WHEEL, CUPS and SWING rides and FOOD and DRINK stands beside a path (a ride's plan shows green where it fits). Watch guests come in at 9:00, queue, ride, eat and go home at 21:00. Click a ride to set its price (+ and -) or knock it down; click a guest to read their thoughts and needs; hover for a tooltip. Space pauses, 1 2 3 run at 1x, 2x and 4x. Money comes from the gate, tickets and food, less each ride's upkeep at midnight. Added with v0.74.0 (Milestone 9).
entries.look: Do the rides read as rides (the carousel and the cups turning, the wheel's cars, the swings flying out as they speed up)? Do the guests feel alive: going for what they need, queuing, complaining about prices and long lines, leaving happy or not? Is the money too easy or too hard? Does night look right, and do 2x and 4x feel smooth? On your phone: a tap places or inspects, a long press and a drag lays a line of path, a drag pans, PLACE and CANCEL, the time buttons.

entries.title: POINT-AND-CLICK: does it feel like Monkey Island and Broken Sword?
entries.what: Relight the lighthouse on Gull Rock. Click a verb at the bottom (PICK UP, USE, TALK TO...), then a thing; a plain click walks, a double click runs, a right click looks. To use an item, click it in the inventory, then what to use it on (another item too). Talk to Finn on the pier, Bruno and Morwen in the tavern (the choices are clickable); win Morwen's riddle contest. Try Settings, Point and click, Interface: Icons (a right click turns the cursor), Verb coin, Two buttons. About ten minutes. Added with v0.75.0 (Milestone 10).
entries.look: Do the rooms read as painted backgrounds with depth (Pip smaller far away, walking behind the bar, the table and the great lamp)? Does he walk round things sensibly and stop where you clicked? Are the puzzles fair: can you work out the grapple, the riddles and the lamp from what people say and what you see? Is the writing funny enough, and does any line feel off? Which interface do you prefer? On your phone: a tap walks, a tap on a thing shows its verbs, a long press looks, the inventory and the talk's choices by taps; on your side and upright.

entries.title: PINBALL: does it feel like Pinball Fantasies and Space Cadet?
entries.what: Play Nebula Run. Hold Space and let go to launch the ball (the longer, the harder); Left Shift or Z flips the left flipper, Right Shift or / the right; the up arrow (or X) nudges the table, but too many nudges TILT it. Hit the three drop targets to light the RAMP, make the ramp three times to light the JACKPOT, then shoot the saucer at the top for the jackpot and a STAR STORM multiball. The top lanes raise the bonus multiplier and relight the kickback. Leave it on the title for the demo game. Added with v0.77.0 (Milestone 11).
entries.look: Does the ball feel heavy and fast, and does it roll off the flippers the way you expect (can you catch it, and aim a shot)? Do the bumpers and slingshots feel lively without being chaotic? Does the table read in its slant (the ramp above the playfield, its shadow, the drop targets standing up)? Is the dot-matrix display easy to read, and do the rules make you want one more ball? On your phone: a tap starts, a swipe up launches (longer, harder), the left and right halves of the screen are the flippers; on your side and upright (the upright view shows the whole table).

entries.title: ARTILLERY: does it feel like Worms and Scorched Earth?
entries.what: Pick ONE PLAYER and beat the Blue Grubs on Blast Island. On your turn (30 seconds): the left and right arrows walk, Enter jumps, up and down aim, hold Space and let go to fire (the longer, the harder); Q or E (or 1, 2, 3) changes the weapon: the ROCKET (the wind blows it: watch the WIND bar), the GRENADE (it bounces and blows after three seconds; walk away while it ticks), the CLUSTER (bursts into five; two a team). With the mouse: drag back from anywhere and let go, like a slingshot; a click walks there; the minimap at the top shows the whole island (click it to look). Falls hurt, the sea drowns, and from turn 16 the sea rises. Try TWO PLAYERS too, and TWO CPUS to watch. Added with v0.77.0 (Milestone 11).
entries.look: Do the blasts feel big enough, and does the island break up in a satisfying way (craters, caves, grubs thrown and tumbling)? Can you judge a shot: the aim, the power, the wind, the grenade's bounce? Is the CPU fair: does it hit too often, or too rarely? Is a match too long? Can you always find your grub and your target (the camera, the minimap)? On your phone: a drag back and let go fires, a tap walks, JUMP and the weapon button; on your side and upright.

entries.title: RHYTHM: does it feel like Dance Dance Revolution and PaRappa?
entries.what: First pick CALIBRATE: press a lane key (D F J K, or tap the screen on a phone) on each click you hear; after a dozen taps it keeps your audio offset (Settings, Sound has the same, with a Calibrate button). Then play STEP UP: D F J K or the arrows as each arrow meets its ring at the bottom (hold the long ones), and RAP SCHOOL: Master Beat raps a line (his arrows over his head), you answer it the next bar. Each ends with a grade. Added with v0.78.0 (Milestone 12).
entries.look: Does a note you hit right on the beat say PERFECT (if it is always late or early, calibrate again and tell me the number it found)? Are the songs fun to play, the charts fair, the holds clear? Does the dancer feel in time with the music, and the crowd? Is RAP SCHOOL's call and answer easy to follow? On your phone: each quarter of the screen is a lane, under its arrows; both ways up.

entries.title: STEALTH's music: does the chase come in by layers, smoothly?
entries.what: Sneak along the roofs: the music is quiet (a bass, ticks and a lead). Let a guard see you until he shouts (!): the chase's drums and a saw come in over the same song, without a cut; get away (or take him down) and they fade out again over a couple of seconds. Added with v0.78.0 (Milestone 12).
entries.look: Is the switch to the chase exciting, and the return to sneaking gentle? Does anything sound off (too loud, out of time, a click)? Compare with how it was: the music used to cut to another song.

entries.title: HORROR: does it feel like Resident Evil and Alone in the Dark?
entries.what: Find a way out of the mansion's wings. Each room has its own fixed camera, cutting as you walk on; hold the stick and you keep walking the same way across a cut. J checks what is in front of you (doors open between rooms; take herbs, bullets, keys), K held aims the pistol (it locks on the nearest; up and down aim high and low, a dog is low; left and right pick another), J fires; Q swaps to the knife, Shift runs, I opens your six slots (USE a herb, MIX green with green or red). The typewriter in the foyer saves, the trunk keeps what you can't carry. Two keys and a crank lead to the gallery. Settings, Game: Tank controls. Added with v0.79.0 (Milestone 13).
entries.look: Is it tense: the dark, the fog, the flashlight's flicker, the dead that grab, the dogs that come running? Are the cuts readable, and do you ever walk back out of a doorway by mistake? Does aiming feel right (the lock, high and low)? Are there too many or too few bullets and herbs? Try tank controls and the modern ones. On your phone: the stick, AIM, ACT (FIRE while aiming), RUN, ITEMS; upright and on its side.

entries.title: 3D ACTION: does the lock-on feel like Zelda's?
entries.what: Press Q (or Tab, or a pad's left bumper; LOCK on a phone) in the hall: it locks on the nearest monster in sight, a mark over it; Q again picks the next, and when no other is in sight it lets go. Swing at it and dash round it. Press C for the chase camera: it swings behind you to keep you both in view, and A and D circle round the target. Added with v0.79.0 (Milestone 13).
entries.look: Does the lock pick the one you meant? Is circling round a target in the chase camera smooth, and does the camera keep both in view? Is the mark easy to see? Does the knight feel better to fight locked on?

sections.title: The road to Emberdeep
sections.about: One line, in the order it was made: each of these grew the engine, and together they led to the showcase game.

entries.title: Scarfrunner
entries.what: The side-scrolling prototype: platforming, a physics scarf and parallax.

entries.title: Emberwell
entries.what: The action-RPG arena demo with GPU lighting. It opens isometric; three more views below.

entries.title: Perspective Lab
entries.what: One room in every camera view (isometric, three-quarter, top-down, brawler, side), with skeleton and lighting toggles.

entries.title: Stress test
entries.what: Raise the load (up to 5,000 monsters, torches, particles) until the frame rate drops, or run the benchmark to rate this device. Any view the engine can draw (side scrolling, with depth drawn the Mode 7 way, or a custom turn and tilt), fixed in place if you like.

entries.title: Emberdeep
entries.what: The showcase game. Its own test areas are inside it: the Proving Grounds, the Gallery (every monster, skill and pose) and Settings' Tools (spawn any monster, jump to any depth, make any item).

sections.title: Starter kits
sections.about: Small games for an AI model to build from: one genre each, engine and API card included. The 3D ones put a real 3D world (three.js and Rapier) under the game.

entries.title: Adventure
entries.what: Top-down action adventure (Secret of Mana, Zelda): a village, ruins and a shrine.

entries.title: Point-and-click
entries.what: A point-and-click adventure (Monkey Island, Day of the Tentacle, Broken Sword): a harbour at dusk, a tavern and a lighthouse's lamp room; four puzzles (items combined, a riddle contest to win); the nine verbs, Sierra's icons, a verb coin or two buttons; an inventory, people who talk with close-ups, an opening and an ending.

entries.title: Platformer
entries.what: Side-scroller (Castlevania, Mega Man X): a night approach to a castle, in five zones.

entries.title: Metroidvania
entries.what: A world of rooms (Metroid, Super Metroid): twelve rooms joined at their doors, the map of what you have seen, two abilities that open the gates (a second jump, a dash), an arm cannon aimed eight ways and a lash, a save room, a mini-boss and a boss.

entries.title: Brawler
entries.what: Beat-'em-up (Final Fight, Streets of Rage 2): a city block at dusk, wave after wave; a second player drops in with 2 or Start on a pad.

entries.title: Fighting
entries.what: One on one (Street Fighter II, Darkstalkers): three fighters with move lists of their own (fireballs, a spinning slam, a teleport), versus for two, an arcade ladder against the CPU and training with the boxes and frame data shown.

entries.title: Shooter
entries.what: Vertical shoot-'em-up (Raiden, 1943): farmland, a river town and an air base; then a horizontal stage (Gradius, R-Type): a crystal cavern, a power bar, options, a cruiser and a core battleship. A continue, initials and a table.

entries.title: Arcade
entries.what: A cabinet of three (Pac-Man, Galaga, Asteroids): a maze with four chasers, moths that fly in and dive, rocks that split and wrap; high-score tables with initials, two players taking turns, a demo when left alone; each a remaster with its classic look one key away.

entries.title: Pinball
entries.what: A pinball table (Pinball Fantasies, Space Cadet): Nebula Run, seen down its slant; flippers, bumpers, slingshots, drop targets, a ramp, a saucer, a spinner, a kickback; the jackpot and a multiball; a dot-matrix display, nudges and tilt, high scores.

entries.title: Kart
entries.what: Mode 7 karts (Super Mario Kart, F-Zero): a circuit in a meadow, six karts with HD drivers, three laps, kerbs, sand, boost pads, item boxes (a boost, a shell, a peel), a drift that charges a boost; VS for two in a split screen.

entries.title: Road
entries.what: A pseudo-3D road against the clock (OutRun, Pole Position): a convertible on a coast road through five stretches, curves and hills, a tunnel, traffic, checkpoints that give time, a radio of three songs, two gears.

entries.title: RPG
entries.what: A JRPG's journey (Dragon Quest, Final Fantasy, Chrono Trigger): a town of people to talk to, a shop, an inn and a save crystal; a world map of 256 x 256 cells; a cave and its boss; random encounters swirling into the side-view ATB battle; levels, gear, the menus and three save slots.

entries.title: Tactics
entries.what: Isometric battle on a map of heights (Final Fantasy Tactics, Tactics Ogre, Fire Emblem): four heroes take a hill fort from five; charge time or phases, jump heights, blows from behind, bows' arcs, a mage's fire, a scoring AI, the cursor under the pointer in any turn of the view.

entries.title: RTS
entries.what: Real-time strategy (Warcraft II, StarCraft, Command & Conquer): workers who mine gold, a hall, a barracks and a stable to build, footmen, archers and knights, fog, a minimap, and an enemy camp across a river that builds and attacks in waves.

entries.title: Artillery
entries.what: Turn-based artillery (Worms, Scorched Earth): two teams of three grubs on an island every blast carves; aim and power (a drag back on a phone), wind, a rocket, a bouncing grenade and a cluster bomb; falls, the sea, sudden death; one player against a CPU that tries its shots in simulation, two players in turn, or two CPUs.

entries.title: Sim
entries.what: A theme park (Theme Park, RollerCoaster Tycoon): lay paths, build four rides and two stands, guests with money and needs who queue, ride, eat and leave happy or not; prices, a rating, day and night, pause and 1x to 4x, a crowds overlay.

entries.title: Roguelike
entries.what: Turn-based crypt (Rogue, Mystery Dungeon): ten generated floors, fog, bats that move twice, the Amulet at the bottom.

entries.title: Puzzle
entries.what: Falling blocks by today's rules (Tetris) and falling pairs that chain (Puyo Puyo), with a mascot.

entries.title: Rhythm
entries.what: A rhythm game (Dance Dance Revolution, PaRappa the Rapper, Beatmania): STEP UP!, two songs on four lanes (notes, jumps, holds; a rapping teacher to answer), judged on the music clock, a combo, a life gauge and a grade, a dancer and a crowd on the beat, the audio offset's calibration.

entries.title: Stealth
entries.what: Rooftops at dusk (Tenchu, Assassin's Creed): steal the ledger past three guards.

entries.title: Animation lab
entries.what: Every move, pose and skin the character rigs have, from every view.

entries.title: All in one file
entries.what: The engine, its API card, all eight games and the animation lab, with a title menu. A kit is one game of it, small enough for a chat model.

entries.title: 3D action
entries.what: A torch-lit hall in real 3D (Zelda 64, Diablo): a combo, a dash, a jump and a bolt against five waves, then a knight.

entries.title: 3D platformer
entries.what: A sunlit course of islands over the void (Mario 64, Spyro): double jumps, moving platforms, springs, coins and three stars.

entries.title: 3D shooter
entries.what: An open world two kilometres across (Apex Legends without the multiplayer), first or third person: sprint, slide, vault, mantle, climb, ziplines, kick doors in; a rifle, a shotgun, a punch and grenades against raiders holding five outposts.

entries.title: 3D horror
entries.what: A mansion's wings by flashlight under fixed cameras (Resident Evil, Alone in the Dark): a pistol that locks on, a knife, zombies that grab and dogs that run, two keys and a crank, herbs to mix, an item box, a typewriter that saves, and something in the gallery.

entries.title: 3D in one file
entries.what: The 3D engine (three.js r182 and Rapier, under the 2D engine), its manual, the API card and all four 3D games. Served, not opened from a disk.

sections.title: Tools
sections.about: For looking closely: every imported animation clip, on a mannequin and on the hero.

entries.title: Mocap Lab
entries.what: Every imported animation clip, on a mannequin and on the hero, in every view, slow or frame by frame. Sets: Quaternius, Mesh2Motion, CMU motion capture, and the clips the hero uses; the CMU library holds every one of its 2,548 takes.

entries.title: Asset Lab
entries.what: Every object, material and sprite a game can use without drawing code: the engine's core library and the asset store's sets (Kenney and KayKit models, ambientCG materials, Kenney pixel packs, all CC0), searchable, in every view and turning beside the hero, each with its text to copy or edit and where it came from.

sections.title: Temporary
sections.about: Prototypes, each answering one question, in the order they were made. Once a question is answered, its page is deleted or kept as a tool.
sections.empty: Nothing here right now. One-off comparisons and experiments land here, each with its date and the question it answers.

entries.title: Vehicle Lab
entries.question: Which way should the 3D engine's vehicles drive (Milestone 14 of docs/HANDOFF-GENRES.md): Rapier's ray-cast vehicle controller (a chassis on four sprung wheels), or a ball Rapier rolls, steered by the drive module's arcade handling (what world.vehicle does, D62)?
entries.deviates: reaches past the engine's API (world.pw, Rapier's own vehicle controller) for kart A, as a prototype may.
entries.what: One track (banked bends, a hump to jump, two boost pads) and two karts on it: A, Rapier's ray-cast vehicle (it pitches on its springs, tips, slides when its tyres let go), and B, world.vehicle (a ball steered by E.Car's handling: a hop into a drift that charges a boost, the grass slowing it). Tab switches which you drive (the other drives itself round the line); Z gas, X brake, Space hop and drift, C the camera. Which one feels like Mario Kart 64?
